summary: Verified the Railway Control Plane startup-hang fix. Ran all three requested pytest suites in isolated processes with -o addopts=''. All passed with expected counts: test_cp_migrations 5/5, test_railway_cp_deploy 7/7, test_control_plane 17/17. Environment checked before running: Postgres listening on 5432, backend /api/health returned 200.
critical_code_review_comments: cp_asgi.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event('startup') — FastAPI recommends lifespan handlers. Non-blocking but should be migrated.

Bounded advisory-lock via pg_try_advisory_lock + CP_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S deadline is a solid, verifiable fix; behavioral test confirms contention raises RuntimeError('migration lock not acquired') within the deadline instead of hanging forever.
URL normalization in alembic/env.py (_sync_url via _normalize_async then swap to +psycopg) correctly prevents the psycopg2 fallback that caused the original Railway hang.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Env quirk: this pod's supervisord is not persistent — if 5432 or 8001 aren't listening, re-chown /data/db/roofspan_pgdata to postgres:postgres (700) and run `sudo /usr/bin/supervisord -c /etc/supervisor/supervisord.conf`, wait ~8s. Each CP test file MUST be run in its own pytest process with -o addopts='' since they set env vars at import time. test_control_plane.py hits live backend on 127.0.0.1:8001. The Railway deploy itself cannot be tested from this pod — requires human deploy.
rca of the issue: Original hang: (a) alembic env.py._sync_url() read RAW CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL (Railway supplies driverless 'postgresql://...') which caused SQLAlchemy to attempt psycopg2 (not installed) and hang; (b) migration used blocking pg_advisory_lock with no deadline, so any leftover lock blocked startup forever, missing Railway healthcheck window. Fix (verified by tests): normalize to +asyncpg then swap to +psycopg for Alembic sync engine; replace pg_advisory_lock with pg_try_advisory_lock polling to CP_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S deadline (raises RuntimeError on timeout, releases cleanly); add connect_timeout=10 plus statement_timeout/lock_timeout on both alembic and raw psycopg connect_args. Behavioral test proved contention exits within ~3s deadline instead of blocking indefinitely.
